report_claim: All measured sections are flattened onto the base of the regional Axel Anderson coal zone at Z = 0 m as a common chronostratigraphic datum (Z_strat = z_measured - z_base_coal).
repository_evidence: Code in smalt/spatial/datum.py does not locate a coal seam or subtract z_base_coal; it reverses measured sections from top to bottom (z = H_max - d) under Prof. Sahoo's provisional rule: 'All litholog zeros should be treated as being at the same reference level.' In Sahoo et al. (2016), the Axel Anderson coal is observed at the base of Cliff Face 1 (L2-L8), but its continuity at L9, L10, L11, and core EM-137C is an unverified correlation assumption. Furthermore, the 2D forward simulator is an unconditioned synthetic generator and does not ingest field datum coordinates.

Document that the formula Z_strat = z_measured - z_base_coal does not exist in code. Clearly separate measured depth, relative stratigraphic elevation, and synthetic model coordinates.

report_claim: Channel sandstone bed thickness follows a validated Log-Normal distribution (MLE mu=1.7870, sigma=0.8823; ordinary KS p=0.8023, Lilliefors bootstrap p=0.4145).
repository_evidence: The ordinary KS test is conservatively biased because parameters were estimated on the test sample. Parameter-estimation-aware Lilliefors bootstrap yields p=0.4196 (continuous) and p=0.6930 (1m discretization). Non-rejection (p > 0.05) does not prove lognormality. In ChannelBeltConfig, thicknesses are truncated to [1.5, 25.0] m, whereas empirical data range from 1.0 to 32.0 m. Crucially, the 34 beds originate from only 8 lithologs (clustered sampling with effective degrees of freedom ~8), yielding a wide 95% confidence interval for mu of [1.498, 2.190] (median thickness 4.47 to 8.94 m).

report_claim: Configured 45% target was intended to match channel sandstone, and the realized 38% sand is an artifact of the stopping rule window and basal planar sand partition.
repository_evidence: In smalt/forward/simulator.py lines 280-286, current_ntg evaluates np.sum(grid == 0) / (nx * nz) (Facies 0, sand alone) and stops when current_ntg >= target_ntg - tolerance (0.45 - 0.08 = 0.37). Across 30 seeds, realized sand averages 38.09% +/- 2.28%. Basal planar sand (p_sand, Facies 1; 20% basal partition) adds 9.46% +/- 1.20%, yielding pure channel-belt sand of 47.55% +/- 3.13%. In Upstream field lithologs, sand alone is 42.94%, while sand + p_sand is 50.52%. The 45% target is an intermediate literature compromise, but the stopping rule ambiguously evaluates single-facies sand against a composite target.
independent_verification_performed: Inspected simulator stopping loop; verified empirical proportions in sprints/audit_sprint_k/litholog_group_facies_proportions.csv; reproduced metrics across 30 seeds.
recommended_resolution: Document semantic ambiguity in ForwardSimulatorConfig: clarify whether target_net_to_gross is an ntg_channel target (empirically 42.9%) or an ntg_pure target (empirically 50.5%). If targeting pure sand, stopping rule should evaluate sand + p_sand. Keep code unchanged during review gate.

report_claim: The downstream preset ripple deficit (5.02% simulated vs 21.15% empirical) is caused by Litholog 9 containing an unusually thick 23.0 m continuous ripple-laminated heterolith unit.
repository_evidence: In data/raw_lithologs/litholog9.csv and sprints/audit_sprint_k/litholog_group_raw_beds.csv, Litholog 9 contains 4 ripple beds with thicknesses 6.0 m, 3.0 m, 2.0 m, and 4.0 m (total ripple thickness 15.0 m). Litholog 11 contains 4 ripple beds with thicknesses 3.0 m, 5.0 m, 7.0 m, and 3.0 m (total ripple thickness 18.0 m). Neither section contains a 23.0 m continuous ripple bed. The simulator deficit is primarily caused by structural limitations of the splay model: splays only attach to channel margins, have maximum thickness 4.5 m, and are eroded by subsequent channels.
independent_verification_performed: Filtered and summed raw bed intervals for L9 and L11; verified absence of any 23m unit; inspected splay placement logic in simulator.py.
recommended_resolution: Retract the claim that Litholog 9 contains a 23.0 m continuous ripple unit. Report true empirical bed thicknesses (max 6.0 m in L9, max 7.0 m in L11). Attribute the downstream ripple deficit to both small-sample variance (N=2 logs) and structural forward simulator constraints (channel-attached splay geometry).

report_claim: Parameters such as 20% basal planar sand fraction, coal thickness (1.0m), and coal horizons (2) are described as 'empirically calibrated' or 'directly measured'.
repository_evidence: In Upstream lithologs, planar sand represents 15.0% of total channel sand (51.0 m / 340.0 m), not 20.0%. Setting basal_fraction = 0.20 is an engineering choice. Upstream logs have 12 coal beds across 8 logs (1.5 beds per 84m log), so placing exactly 2 continuous horizontal sheets at relative elevations [0.25, 0.75] is a modeling assumption. Splay widths [20, 100] m and channel W/T = 35 +/- 5 are regional literature priors from Sahoo et al. (2016), not site-calibrated constants.
